relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with SSADH deficiency and Rett syndrome: "The proband was compound heterozygous for pathogenic ALDH5A1 mutations".
method_note: Read the paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON and asserted every span verbatim. Labels: the paper calls the patient only 'the proband'/'our patient' (role words), so rule 5 'patient'; Table 1 parents labelled 'mother of patient' and 'father of patient'. Table 1 (WES of proband and parents) has patients/relatives as rows; cells contain line breaks, so some spans run across the newline in the cell. The maternal ALDH5A1 variant is printed as 'NM_001080.3:g.1253del' (a g. description on an NM_ transcript, with colon), while the paternal one uses a semicolon ('NM_001080.3;c.1226G>A'); both recorded exactly as printed, the first in genomic_coordinates_as_stated with cdna null. Inconsistency: Table 1 zygosity column lists 'Hz' for each proband ALDH5A1 row while the abstract says 'compound heterozygous'; the abstract statement names the proband and was used. Table 1 parent MECP2 rows read 'Hz, XL' in the zygosity column but 'Not detected' in the comment column; interpreted as the MECP2 variant not detected in either parent (consistent with 'de novo' in the abstract), so no MECP2 rows for the parents. The table note 'all variants are predicted to be pathogenic' is a general statement and was not used; proband ALDH5A1 pathogenicity comes from the abstract sentence naming the proband; MECP2 and parental pathogenicity left not reported. Variant type for ALDH5A1 variants not stated ('Protein termination' comment is not a class), so not reported. EEG: initial EEG at 28 months normal (excluded row 'abnormal EEG' with detail), follow-up at 36 months abnormal; this is change over time, not a contradiction, so checklist EEG item = observed. MRI 'slight prominence of the sulci raising suspicion for mild, diffuse parenchymal volume loss' is hedged: recorded as observed sulcal prominence, checklist atrophy left not reported. 'Does not exhibit any of the characteristic social delays often present in autism spectrum disorder' recorded as excluded feature, but the broader checklist item autism spectrum disorder or autistic behaviors left not reported (she has hand stereotypies; narrow absence does not exclude broad item). Intellectual disability not stated for the patient (only global developmental delay), so not reported. Vital status not explicitly stated; left not reported. Age at last evaluation taken from 'During the first 3.5 years of development'. Parents have no phenotype statements; all checklist items not reported. No stacked ' / ' cells in this paper.
